title: acme-enterprise-integration-call-notes-2026-03-03
body:
ACME Enterprise — Integration call notes (quick working notes)
Date: 2026-03-03
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood CS), Maya Rodriguez (Redwood Solutions), Ethan Wang (Redwood SE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood PM),
           Laura Chen (ACME SRE), Diego Ramirez (ACME Product), Priyanka Sen (ACME SecOps)

Purpose: capture ACME requirements/gotchas for connecting to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated, clarify SLA/latency targets, and list next steps + owners. This is a scratchpad for follow-up — not final doc.

High-level summary / ask from ACME:
- They want predictable p99 latency <= 250ms for chat completions for core product flows (~80% requests).
- Data residency: EU-only for PII flows, global for analytics. Need VPC/private option for EU-sensitive traffic.
- Strong requirement for KMS/HSM integration + audit logs for model inputs for a subset of customers.
- Expected traffic: 200 TPS peak (burst to 400 TPS) for embeddings + chat combined during campaign windows.
- Want ability to pin model family and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants when Dedicated capacity is exhausted.

Notes / clarifications we gave:
- Hosted (default): fastest time-to-value, but no dedicated capacity SLA. We proposed Redwood Dedicated for guaranteed throughput + isolation.
- Dedicated offers autoscaling policies + burst capacity (can model economics in a follow-up doc). We outlined default batching behaviors and how that affects latency.
- VPC/private: we can offer private control plane + on-prem connector; will need network prep from ACME (subnets, NAT, egress rules).

Technical gotchas ACME raised / we should track:
- KMS/HSM: ACME uses AWS KMS with external key management; they require proof of key separation and rotation policy compatibility. Action: Maya to confirm KMS integration checklist.
- Large context windows: their product sometimes sends 16k tokens. Need to validate model + quantization profile; may require special kernel selection. Action: Ethan to run a perf estimate for 16k sequence lengths across candidate models.
- Embedding throughput: embeddings are batched differently; ACME expects near-linear scaling. Need to validate batching config and memory limits.
- Logging & PII: they want input redaction option and separate audit stream for PII events. We currently have audit logs + token-level cost traces — need product note on configurable redaction + retention.

SLA / Ops specifics discussed:
- ACME asked for a 99.9% uptime target, with p99 latency SLO for API (250ms). We suggested a hybrid: Dedicated for mission-critical flows + Hosted fallback for overflow.
- Circuit-breaker policy: automatic fallback to smaller model family if Dedicated capacity unavailable — must be explicit in their runbook.
- Pagination of KV cache: some of their use-cases re-use long prefixes; need to test KV cache eviction behavior at scale.

Security / compliance notes:
- They require SOC2 + ISO27001 (we are ok). Also asked for a pen-test report. Maya to attach compliance pack.
- Data residency: for EU-only flows we recommended deploying Dedicated capacity in EU region or using Private deployment.
- Contractual: they want an indemnity clause for data breaches; legal to escalate.

Immediate action items (owners + rough ETA):
1) Maya: KMS/HSM integration checklist + compliance pack (SOC2, pen-test) — ETA 2026-03-10.
2) Ethan: perf matrix for candidate models (open-llama-13B, redwood-default-7B, redwood-quant-8bit) at 2048/8192/16384 token lengths; include latency + GPU mem + cost estimates — ETA 2026-03-09.
3) Samir: draft high-level Dedicated sizing proposal (200 TPS baseline, 400 TPS burst) with cost ballpark and autoscale policy options — ETA 2026-03-08.
4) Priya: product note on audit logs + redaction options + retention settings; include sample retention policy language for contract — ETA 2026-03-11.
5) Maya + Laura (ACME): Network prep checklist for VPC — exchange subnets + NAT + firewall rules. Maya to set up a shared Confluence page.
6) Samir: create JIRA INF ticket for "ACME Dedicated onboarding" and link required PRs + runbooks. (JIRA key INF-2412) — ETA 2026-03-05.

Follow-ups we promised on the call:
- Live demo of dedicated cluster provisioning and canary rollout (Samir / Ethan) — propose week of 2026-03-15.
- Share example canary rollout config (A/B weighting + auto-fallback) and a sample runbook for circuit-breaker behaviors.
- Short deck for legal covering KMS/keys, data flows, and audit logs (Maya).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Exact encryption-at-rest key flow when using Dedicated in ACME VPC vs hosted (who holds keys for backups?). Need infra input.
- Do they want model logging turned on for all requests or only to flagged customers? Need contractual clarity.
- What is acceptable cold-start latency for their product when we scale up new workers? (they implied under 1s)

Quick links referenced on call:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ACME-INTEGRATION-PLATFORM-REQS (private)
- JIRA: INF-2412 (onboarding epic)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/acme-infra-provisioning/pull/12 (initial terraform module skeleton)

Notes for follow-up email to ACME (to-do once internal items above confirmed):
- Recap what we heard + summarize Dedicated sizing + cost estimate + suggested timeline.
- Provide checklist for network/VPC prep and data residency options.
- Propose two dates for live demo / provisioning walkthrough.

Misc scratch bits (internal):
- Potential risk: their 16k token use combined with high TPS could require >1TB GPU mem if not quantized / sharded — likely need to push them to quantized variants or multi-GPU sharding.
- Consider offering a pilot: 4-week Dedicated pilot with 99.5% uptime SLA, capped token spend — helps unblock procurement.

Next update: will refresh this doc after Maya/ Ethan deliver artifacts.

-- Samir

(Internal tag: user-notes, informal. Move into shared_drives/customer-success once we have a proposal & pricing sheet.)
